commits.subject: Set USE_TYPO_METRICS, as the release has
commits.body: The release sets fsSelection bit 7 (USE_TYPO_METRICS); it was built with sfdLib 2.0.0, which sets it whenever OS2_UseTypoMetrics is present. This file says 0.

commits.subject: Set the full name the release has
commits.body: The release was built with sfdLib 2.0.0 and ufo2ft 3.4.1, which write name ID 4 as the family and style names (Comic Relief Regular); FontForge exports FullName, which this file states as Comic Relief.

commits.subject: State the outline sfdLib 2.0.0 read from sources/ComicRelief-Regular.sfd
commits.body:
The release (google/fonts 0ed65319a ofl/comicrelief/ComicRelief-Regular.ttf, from loudifier/Comic-Relief 856315f5) was built with sfdLib 2.0.0 and ufo2ft, not exported by FontForge. In a quadratic layer FontForge flags an on-curve point it can leave implied (midway between its two control points) with 0x80, SFD_PTFLAG_INTERPOLATE; sfdLib 2.0.0 writes every such point as an OFF-curve point at the same place, and when a contour's closing segment is flagged, its first point too (Lib/sfdLib/parser.py _drawContours, line 394: 'if flag & 0x80: ... ufoContour.append((pt, None, None))', under 'XXX I don't know what I'm doing'). The release's outlines carry that: three control points in a row where this file has control, on-curve, control.

This file has 30 such points in 22 glyphs. Each one becomes a control point at the same place, and the on-curve points TrueType implies between two adjacent control points are written out at their exact midpoints, flagged 0x80 with TrueType number -1, as FontForge stores implied points. A contour whose first point becomes a control point starts at its first remaining on-curve point instead, where the release's contour starts. The point made a control point gets an unused TrueType number; every other point keeps its own.

Without the added implied points this is sfdLib's point list exactly, and that list, rounded as ufo2ft rounds, is the release's glyf in all 22 glyphs (sfd-reland tools/probes/exporter_source_edits/sfdlib_outline_check.py). No other glyph changes.

commits.subject: Set UnderlinePosition so the build gets the release's -97
commits.body: Both released styles have post.underlinePosition -97 and underlineThickness 175. sfdLib 2.0.0 moved this file's UnderlinePosition -185 up by half the UnderlineWidth 175 ('FontForge does not match OpenType here', parser.py), giving -97.5, which ufo2ft rounded to -97. These sources are converted with babelfont's --fontforge-underline-position, the rule of FontForge's exporter up to tag 20170731: position - width/2, truncated toward zero, which turns -185 into -272. UnderlinePosition -10 is the value that rule turns into the release's -97 (-10 - 87.5 = -97.5, truncated); UnderlineWidth stays 175. The build's underline is the release's (top -97, 175 thick); the number stated here is no longer its centre, which is what FontForge's UnderlinePosition means.

flags_reason: --fontforge-notdef dropped: the release was built with sfdLib 2.0.0 and a UFO compiler, not exported by FontForge, and its .notdef is not FontForge's rectangle (research-scratch sfd-reland-notdef/notdef_census.py). --round-coordinates dropped: it reproduces FontForge's exporter, which rounds each coordinate to even (rint) as it writes it; this release's glyf was compiled by ufo2ft, which rounds half up (otRound) after decomposing components, as fontc does when the converter leaves the coordinates as stated. Built from these sources (sfd-reland tools/probes/exporter_source_edits/comic_build_check.py), the glyph outlines that differ from the release's are 9 in ComicRelief-Regular and 8 in ComicRelief-Bold without it, 15 and 211 with it (9 and 31 with the babelfont filter the sfdlibinterpolated edit replaces).
